check: EventBus worker, alert handler, and durable loopback notification retry across disposable PostgreSQL stop/start
limitations: Only the event, durable-handler, and notification table migrations were replayed in the disposable database; the full ordered schema ledger was not applied.

The real allowlisted alert-notification handler ran in its spawned child process. A temporary HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1 received all three notification requests; no remote provider was contacted.

The local server returned one synthetic 503, then accepted the retry and the post-restart notification. The first notification attempt was durably marked failed with the outbox retryable, then recovered to succeeded with its latest attempt succeeded; the retry reused the same durable notification ID as its idempotency key.

A third notification request was received while its worker was blocked before receiving the HTTP response. The process was killed, its lease expired in the fixture, and a one-shot replacement worker reclaimed it; the attempt history was lease_lost then succeeded, and the duplicate request reused the same idempotency key.
All five loopback requests carried their matching durable notification IDs as idempotency keys; retries reused the source notification ID, while the three source events used distinct IDs.
The PostgreSQL container had no volume and was bound only to loopback.
